name: Cancel or redirect a US trip, and say why
shortDescription: Inbound tourism is counted and published monthly.
longDescription: Travel is the one category with a public scoreboard: arrivals and tourism receipts are reported as national statistics. Cancelling or redirecting a trip registers there — and telling the airline, hotel or tourist board why turns a data point into a stated reason.

name: Take the train instead of a short-haul flight
shortDescription: Under about five hours, the train usually wins door to door.
longDescription: Once you count airport transfer, security and boarding, most European city pairs under 700km are faster by rail. Booking direct with the national operator also avoids a platform fee.

name: Book a night train
shortDescription: Replaces a flight and a hotel night at once.
longDescription: Europe's sleeper network has expanded considerably — Nightjet, European Sleeper and Snälltåget now connect most of the continent. Booking one removes a flight from the count and a hotel night from the bill.

name: Get an Interrail or Eurail pass
shortDescription: Prepays a season of travel onto European rail.
longDescription: A pass commits a block of travel spending to European rail operators up front, and tends to change how you plan trips for the rest of the year — flights stop being the default option because the rail is already paid for.

name: Holiday in Europe this year
shortDescription: The whole trip, not one leg of it.
longDescription: Choosing a European destination for your main holiday moves flights, accommodation, food and local spending together. It's the single largest discretionary redirect most households make in a year, which is why it's worth checking in on rather than logging once.

name: Fly a European carrier instead of a US one
shortDescription: When you do fly, the airline is still a choice.
longDescription: On transatlantic and intra-European routes there is nearly always a European operator on the same city pair, often codesharing the identical flight. Booking the European metal keeps the fare with the European carrier.

name: Book your hotel direct instead of through a platform
shortDescription: Booking.com is US-owned. Most people assume otherwise.
longDescription: Booking.com reads as European because of the Amsterdam office and the .com trading name, but it is owned by Booking Holdings, a US company headquartered in Connecticut — as are Kayak, Priceline, Agoda and OpenTable. Booking direct with the hotel avoids a commission that commonly runs 15–20% of the room rate, and hotels will usually match or beat the platform price if you ask.

name: Skip Airbnb for a local guesthouse or Fairbnb
shortDescription: A pension, a guesthouse, or a cooperative platform.
longDescription: Independent guesthouses and small hotels keep the whole rate, and cooperative platforms return a share of their commission to local projects. In most European cities this is also the cheaper option once cleaning and service fees are counted.

name: Rent from a European car company
longDescription: Hertz, Avis, Budget and Enterprise are US groups; Sixt and Europcar are European and operate the same airport and city desks at comparable rates.

name: Use a national tourist board instead of a US platform
shortDescription: Better information, no commission, no tracking.
longDescription: National and regional tourist boards publish the same accommodation, transport and event listings the platforms aggregate, and usually link straight to the operator. Planning from there avoids feeding a booking platform's ranking data.

name: Take the coach instead
shortDescription: The cheapest way to not take a flight.
longDescription: Long-distance coaches cover routes rail doesn't and undercut both rail and air on price. For a short hop it's the lowest-cost substitution available.

name: Tell an operator why you changed your booking
shortDescription: Cancellations are counted. Reasons are not, unless you give one.
longDescription: Airlines, hotels and booking platforms all run cancellation surveys and none of them infer motive. A sentence in the feedback box or a short email to customer relations puts your reason into a dataset someone reports on.
